10.1002_adfm.202516265: All‐solid‐state thin film lithium‐ion microbatteries (TFBs) are regarded as the ideal on‐board power sources for microelectronic devices. However, the indispensable high preparation temperature (≥500 °C) required for commonly used cathodes, coupled with the Li anode's low melting point and high chemical reactivity, restricts TFBs’ on‐chip integration and high‐temperature operational capabilities. In this work, a Li x MnO 2 /LiPON/Nb 2 O 5‐x configuration (LMN‐TFB), featuring a low preparation temperature (180 °C) and exceptional chemical and thermal stability, is proposed to simultaneously enable a wide operational temperature range and on‐chip multilayer integration. The LMN‐TFB exhibits a reversible capacity of 26.5 µAh cm −2 and a long cycle life (83.5% capacity retention after 1500 cycles) at room temperature, as well as adequate working ability in a wide temperature range between ‐20 and 210 °C. Moreover, the integration of multilayer stacked LMN‐TFBs on a chip allows for increased capacity (37.5 µAh cm −2 ) or higher working voltage (6.5 V) than the individual LMN‐TFB, resulting in increased areal energy densities within the limited footprint area without significantly increasing the volume or weight. This work presents a promising approach for constructing integratable and wide‐temperature TFBs, offering significant potential for on‐board microelectronic devices.
10.1002_adma.74630: High‐entropy Prussian blue analogues (PBAs) are promising cathodes for sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs). However, inherent [Fe(CN) 6 ] 4– defects deteriorate electrochemical kinetics and phase stability. Herein, an unusual cyanide (CN – ) vacancy is tailored in high‐entropy PBA (HE‐Cu‐PA, Na 1.58 Mn 0.191 Fe 0.2 Co 0.195 Ni 0.2 Cu 0.19 [Fe(CN) 5.85 ]), constructed via a phytic acid (PA) assisted coprecipitation method, as cathode material for SIBs. The precisely designed high‐entropy composition with CN – defects create adaptive coordination flexible sites and local electronic delocalization regions, synergistically enhancing structural stability, electrochemical dynamics, and redox reversibility. The large‐sized [Fe(CN) 6 ] 4– vacancy in PA‐free high‐entropy PBA (HE‐Cu) exhibits poor electronic transfer capability and accumulated lattice strain, while static local lattice distortion generated by Ti 3+ N 6 octahedron in high‐entropy composition (HE‐Ti‐PA) causes large lattice stress and Na‐ion diffusion barrier. The complex structural evolution (monoclinic ↔ cubic ↔ tetragonal) originated from Jahn–Teller effect and octahedron instability can be completely restrained in HE‐Cu‐PA, achieving a zero‐strain solid‐solution Na‐ion storage mechanism, where Mn, Fe, Co, and Cu‐ions act as redox sites for charge compensation. Therefore, HE‐Cu‐PA delivers high initial capacity of 117.6 mAh·g −1 , superior rate capability and ultra‐long lifespan over 6000 cycles with ultra‐low decay‐rate of 0.0085% per cycle. And ultra‐long cycling lifetime over 4000 cycles can be acquired for high‐energy‐density (338.0 Wh·kg −1 ) quasi‐solid‐state Na‐ion full batteries.
10.1002_eem2.70236: Aqueous‐based zinc‐iodine batteries (AZIBs) are extremely competitive and have gigantic potential in the next generation of energy storage technologies on account of their ultra‐high safety and excellent theoretical capacity. Howbeit, the unsatisfactory conductivity of iodine and the shuttle effect of polyiodides will greatly confine their commercial applications. In this study, an original composite material of selenium (Se) and activated carbon (AC) (designated as Se–AC), as a functional iodine‐adsorbed cathode host, is successfully synthesized with the dual‐effect function of Se. Se has a larger atomic size and higher polarizability compared to carbon, effectively accelerating the charge transfer rate. Therefore, the incorporation of Se nanoparticles can generate higher strain at the edge of AC to improve the adsorption of iodine species, especially I 3 − . Furthermore, the inorganic Se nanoparticles can make AC provide abundant adsorption‐catalytic active sites that significantly enhance electron transfer kinetics while catalyzing the I 0 /I − conversion reaction. As expected, Se–AC/I 2 can deliver an ideal specific capacity of 249.7 mAh g −1 at 0.1 A g −1 . Additionally, the energy density of Se–AC/I 2 //Zn exhibits 217.5 Wh kg −1 at 86.2 W kg −1 , exceeding most reported AZIBs. This dual‐effect function strategy creates transformative opportunities for AZIBs, enabling high energy density, long cycling, and cost‐effective energy storage solutions for renewable grids.
10.1016_j.apsusc.2026.166536: • Controlled reduction creates Pt-reduced nanoparticles and surface defects. • Exsolved ∼1.2 nm Pt-reduced nanoparticles boost oxygen electrocatalysis. • Distribution of relaxation times analysis indicated enhanced charge transfer. • Post-mortem O K-edge XAS suggested surface restructuring due to Pt exsolution. This work explores the exsolution of well-dispersed nanoparticles containing reduced Pt species from La 0.6 Sr 0.4 Fe 0.95 Pt 0.05 O 3-δ (LSFPt) as an effective approach to design catalysts for oxygen electrocatalysis. A 10 h reduction treatment at 500 °C in 5% H 2 /Ar promotes the exsolution of ∼1.2 nm Pt nanoparticles on the surface, increasing oxygen deficiency without compromising the perovskite structure. The resulting catalyst exhibits over 2.5-fold performance improvement for oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and reduction reaction (ORR) in alkaline media compared to the as-prepared LSFPt. Specifically, OER potential decreased from 1.61 to 1.58 V RHE , while the ORR potential improved from 0.31 to 0.48 V RHE . Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), combined with distribution of relaxation times (DRT) deconvolution analysis, revealed a notable decrease in medium-frequency resistance, indicating enhanced charge transfer at the electrode surface for OER and ORR. Post-mortem O K-edge spectra obtained by soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy in total electron yield mode further suggest an increased surface restructuring in the reduced LSFPt, attributed to the synergistic presence of surface defects and exsolved nanoparticles containing reduced Pt species. This one-step reduction protocol provides a valuable methodological insight for designing catalysts for oxygen electrocatalysis by tailoring the surface composition of perovskite material aligned with the necessity for bifunctional systems.
10.1016_j.est.2025.120262: Electric vehicles are prime for the energy transition, but their lithium-ion batteries are not carbon-neutral. To decrease their environmental impacts, it is essential to increase their lifespan. For this purpose, temperature can play a major role. This paper suggests an approach to assess the potential lifespan and environmental savings of various improvements of battery thermal management. To this end, an electro-thermal model coupled with degradation models of three different battery pack chemistries (NMC/LMO, NMC and LFP), in three different climates, and with real-world driving conditions, was developed. It showed that optimizing the heat transfer pathways in the battery pack could lead to a maximum of 20% lifespan increase. The model also showed that capacity losses in parking phases account for 62% to 83% of total battery degradation. Therefore, solutions tackling calendar losses, for example cooling the pack during parking phases, can lead to 87% lifespan increase in a warm climate. Life Cycle Assessment showed that this solution could decrease greenhouse gases emissions over the life cycle of the vehicle by up to 29%. Therefore, parkcooling of battery packs seems a more relevant solution than improving the thermal contact in order to decrease the environmental impacts of battery packs.
10.1021_acsnano.6c15505: Aqueous zinc–iodine (Zn–I2) batteries are highly promising for grid-scale energy storage, yet their practical viability is severely plagued by the polyiodides shuttle effect and sluggish liquid–solid conversion kinetics, which fundamentally arise from the contradictory energetic demands between soluble intermediate confinement and solid-product desorption. Herein, we rationally construct a dual-facet spinel cobalt oxide to precisely decouple these competing interfacial behaviors. By regulating the proportional exposure of strongly coordinating (100) and weakly coordinating (111) facets, a tailored surface microenvironment is constructed that effectively circumvents the inherent thermodynamic trade-off, breaking the single adsorption limitation intrinsic to uniform catalysts. In situ iodine L3-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy and three-dimensional synchrotron-based nanocomputed tomography reveal that this specific facet modulation substantially reduces the activation barrier for rate-determining polyiodides oxidation, facilitating spatially uniform solid-iodine deposition. Driven by these structural advantages, the assembled Zn–I2 batteries with c/o-Co3O4 deliver a high specific capacity of 161.1 mAh g–1 at 16 A g–1 and an ultralow capacity decay rate of 0.00055% per cycle after 50,000 cycles at 10 A g–1. Furthermore, the batteries also exhibit a broad operational temperature ranging from −30 to 60 °C, highlighting the strong potential for practical applications. This work provides a perspective on facet engineering for achieving wide-temperature-tolerant aqueous iodine storage.
10.1038_s41467-026-78068-w: The rapid advancement of reticular chemistry has enabled the synthesis of thousands of covalent organic framework (COF) powders bearing various structures and functions. Nevertheless, processing these COF powders into application-ready membranes with precise separation capacity remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a dynamic covalent chemistry-based dual-drive strategy is harnessed to drive macroscopic structural variation, achieving the transformation of powdered COFs into defect-free COF membranes. This powder-to-membrane transformation is enabled by the internal factor of framework reconstruction and the external driving force of acid attack, showcasing high processibility, which affords scalable two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) COF membranes with a maximum area of 225 cm2. The optimum TpPa membrane demonstrates excellent performance in molecular sieving, displaying high rejections towards dye (99%) and pharmaceutical molecules (98%) and a pure water permeance of 179.0 L m−2 h−1 bar−1. Moreover, our dual-drive transformation outperforms conventional methods in fabrication efficiency, conversion ratio, separation performance, etc., offering a green, efficient, versatile, and scalable strategy for the preparation and application of COF membranes in chemical engineering separations. Processing covalent organic framework (COF) powders into application-ready membranes with precise separation capacity remains challenging. Here, the authors demonstrate a dual-drive strategy that drives macroscopic structural variation and transforms COF powders into defect-free membranes.
10.1039_d5ee07558k: Thermally regenerative flow batteries (TRFBs) offer a promising route for harvesting low-grade waste heat; however, their power output is limited by the mismatch in redox reaction kinetics during the reverse reactions between the cold and hot cells.
